board.name: West Virginia Board of Medicine (PAs collaborating with osteopathic physicians may instead be licensed by the WV Board of Osteopathic Medicine)

licence.title: Physician Assistant (PA; PA-C only while NCCPA certified)
licence.renewalDeadline: Biennial; all PA licences renew before April 1 of every odd year (expire March 31 of odd years; last cycle closed March 31, 2025, next March 31, 2027). No grace period for practice after expiration.

ce.categoryRules: 100 hours per two year reporting period. Category I or II from AMA, AAPA or AAFP; Category II capped at 50 hours (board page: minimum 50 Category I). Alternatives: passing an NCCPA recertification exam in the period, or a PA master's degree within one year of initial licence expiry (each worth 100 hours, or 97 if the 3 hour controlled substance course is mandatory). The board's CME page also says the 3 hour controlled substance course can be used for 3 of the 50 Category I hours.
ce.nccpaNote: Holding NCCPA certification alone does not satisfy CME. Only PASSING an NCCPA recertification examination during the reporting period substitutes for the 100 hours, and it never substitutes for the 3 hour controlled substance course.
ce.nccpaRenewalNote: Current NCCPA certification (or a licence from a state not requiring it) is required for initial licensure under W. Va. Code 30-3E-4(b)(5); at renewal the PA only reports NCCPA status, and a PA whose certification lapsed may renew using the designation PA.

topicMandates.topic: Risk Assessment and Responsible Prescribing of Controlled Substances (drug diversion, best practice prescribing, opioid antagonist training), board approved course
topicMandates.appliesTo: PAs who prescribed, administered or dispensed any controlled substance under a WV licence during the reporting period; counts toward the 100 hours

topicMandates.topic: Same 3 hour board approved controlled substance course within one year of initial licensure
topicMandates.appliesTo: Newly licensed PAs who prescribe, administer or dispense controlled substances under a WV licence

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 3 hours board approved course every biennial reporting period for anyone who prescribed, administered or dispensed a controlled substance under a WV licence (11 CSR 1B 14.4); waived for those who did not. The DEA 8 hour MATE training counts only if that course is on the board approved list.

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: PA may not practise independently and practises in collaboration with physicians under a practice notification filed jointly by the PA and a health care facility with the board ($100 fee), activated only on the board's written notice. It terminates automatically if the licence expires, the PA leaves the listed facility, or loses credentials there; the PA must notify the board in writing within 10 days of a termination. No periodic renewal of the notification is stated; the PA attests at licence renewal to practising within it.
practice.notes: Practice agreements authorized before June 1, 2021 ended by June 1, 2022 (W. Va. Code 30-3E-9). Prescriptive authority comes with an active practice notification; no Schedule I; Schedule II narcotics limited to a 3 day supply.

prescribing.separateAuthorityRegistration: No separate state controlled substance registration for prescribing. Registration with the WV Controlled Substances Monitoring Program (Board of Pharmacy) is required for practitioners who prescribe or dispense Schedule II to V, within 30 days of a new licence. Office based administering or dispensing of controlled substances (including samples) requires a board Controlled Substance Dispensing Practitioner Registration, renewed with the licence.
prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 3 hour board approved controlled substance course each biennium (see topicMandates).
prescribing.stateCsRegistrationNote: Not yet verified. W. Va. Code 60A-3-302(a) requires an annual registration from the Board of Pharmacy 'or the appropriate department, board, or agency' for anyone who dispenses a controlled substance, and 60A-1-101 defines dispense to include prescribing. The Board of Pharmacy permit page cites an exemption in 15 CSR 2-3.2 that was not loaded. The WV Board of Osteopathic Medicine issues a Controlled Substance License to DOs. Whether a WV PA needs a state CS registration to prescribe is therefore unconfirmed; the board's renewal FAQ names only CSMP registration and the office dispensing registration.

pa.osteopathicBoardNote: PAs licensed by the WV Board of Osteopathic Medicine (24 CSR 2): the only rule text the board links is a 2019 emergency amendment. It shows 100 hours per 2 years with at least 50 Category 1 written into the rule, AOA credit accepted, no NCCPA recertification exam pathway listed, and the 3 hour drug diversion course required also of anyone practising under an active practice notification. The current legislative rule was not loaded, so these differences are not yet verified.

board.name: West Virginia Board of Registered Nurses (WV RN Board)

rn.renewalDeadline: June 30 of each even numbered year
rn.nclNote: WV has enacted the Nurse Licensure Compact (W. Va. Code 30-7F).

topicMandates.topic: Drug diversion training, best practice prescribing of controlled substances and opioid antagonist training
topicMandates.appliesTo: Newly licensed RNs/APRNs who prescribe, administer or dispense a controlled substance; within 1 year of initial licence (waiver available if none)

rn.notes: A nurse first licensed in WV during a reporting period is exempt from CE for that period (19 CSR 11 3.2.1). 12 of the APRN's 24 hours may count toward the RN 12.

aprn.title: APRN plus designated role title (e.g. Nurse Practitioner); licence issued by the WV RN Board
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: Separate APRN licence (on top of WV RN licence or NLC multistate privilege), plus separate prescriptive authority
aprn.renewalDeadline: Renewal period runs July 1 of an odd year to June 30 of the next odd year (expires June 30, odd years)
aprn.ceSplit: 24 contact hours per cycle: 12 in pharmacotherapeutics and 12 in clinical management of patients

topicMandates.topic: Drug diversion, best practice prescribing of controlled substances and opioid antagonist training
topicMandates.appliesTo: APRNs who prescribe, administer or dispense controlled substances; within 1 year of initial licensure

prescribing.separateAuthorityRegistration: Yes. Limited prescriptive authority is a separate board authorization (identification number), renewed biennially; initial eligibility needs 45 contact hours in pharmacology and clinical management of drug therapy, 15 of them within the 2 years immediately before entering the prerequisite collaborative relationship (W. Va. Code 30-7-15b(a)(3)).
prescribing.pharmacologyCeForPrescribers: 8 contact hours of board approved pharmacology in the 2 years before renewal of prescriptive authority; may be part of the APRN licence's 12 pharmacotherapeutics hours.
prescribing.controlledSubstanceCe: 3 hours drug diversion/best practice prescribing/opioid antagonist within 1 year of initial licensure (one-time per the board page and W. Va. Code 30-1-7a). No Schedule I; Schedule II narcotics limited to a 3 day supply.
prescribing.csNote: No separate WV CS registration for prescribing is NOT confirmed (see the PA note: 60A-3-302 and the unloaded 15 CSR 2-3.2 exemption). Confirmed: DEA registration numbers are filed with the RN Board (19 CSR 8 3.8) and CSMP registration is required for Schedule II to V prescribers (W. Va. Code 60A-9-5a(a)).

practice.transitionNote: Transition is time based, not hours: a written collaborative agreement with a physician is required for prescriptive authority until the APRN has practised at least 3 years in a documented collaborative relationship with prescriptive authority, then may apply to prescribe without one.
practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Verification of the written collaborative agreement is filed with the RN Board, which forwards it to the Board of Medicine or Osteopathic Medicine. If the agreement dissolves with no other current agreement, the APRN must stop prescribing immediately and has 60 days to file a new verified agreement before a reinstatement application is required.
